title: Percentiles
objective: After this level you can explain what being in the 90th percentile means, using children's growth charts and test scores.
summary: A percentile is a place in ordered data: at the 90th percentile, 90% of values are the same or lower. Growth charts compare a child with others of the same sex and age.

cards.headline: "Your child is in the 90th percentile." That's not a score out of 100.
cards.body: It is not a grade at all. It is a position in a line of other children, and once you picture the line, the number makes sense.

cards.headline: Your place in a line of 100
cards.body: Line up a set of values in order and cut it into hundredths: those cuts are percentiles. Like a percent, a percentile works out of every 100. Scoring in the 90th percentile on an exam does not mean you got 90% right. It means 90% of the scores were the same as or below yours.

cards.headline: What a growth chart is saying
cards.body: Growth charts use percentiles to compare a child with children of the same sex and age. On the CDC's charts, a 5-year-old girl at the 25th percentile for weight weighs the same as or more than 25% of 5-year-old girls, and less than the other 75%. It is a position, not a verdict: the chart says where she stands in the line.

cards.context: Level 12's middle value has half the data on each side, so it sits exactly at the 50th percentile. The 25th and 75th percentiles have names too: the lower and upper quartiles. Together they turn one number into a place in the crowd.

cards.headline: Percentiles: your place in line
learned: Percentiles cut ordered data into hundredths
Growth charts compare same sex and age

questions.prompt: What does scoring in the 90th percentile on an exam mean?

options.label: You got 90% of the questions right
options.rationale: That is a percent score, not a percentile.

options.label: 90% of scores were the same as or below yours
You were one of the top 90 students
options.rationale: A percentile is a share of everyone, not a count of places.

options.label: You beat the average score by 90 points
options.rationale: A percentile is a position, not a margin.

questions.explanation: A percentile is a position: at the 90th, 90% of scores were the same as or below yours.

questions.prompt: A 5-year-old girl is at the 25th percentile for weight. Who is she being compared with?

options.label: Every child her doctor has ever seen
options.rationale: Growth charts compare with a reference group of the same sex and age.

options.label: Adults of the same height
options.rationale: The comparison is with children of her own sex and age.

options.label: Other 5-year-old girls in the reference group
Her own weight a year earlier
options.rationale: A percentile compares her with other children, not with herself.

questions.explanation: She weighs the same as or more than 25% of 5-year-old girls in the reference group, and less than 75%.

questions.prompt: Level 12's median sits at which percentile?

options.label: The 100th
options.rationale: That would be the very top.

options.label: The 90th
options.rationale: The median is in the middle, not near the top.

questions.explanation: The median has half the values on each side, so it is the 50th percentile.
